737 Chrome VPN Extensions Caught Routing Traffic Through Proxies. Check If You Have One

The Hacker News
2026-08-12 9 use cases 3 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A massive set of 737 free VPN and proxy extensions have been found to mainly target Russian-speaking users seeking access to blocked services with an aim to intercept browser traffic and route them through a proxy infrastructure. The extensions, published across at least 40 Chrome Web Store developer accounts, racked up 75,486 installs. Of those identified, 274 have been found to impersonate 66

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation · Article-specific behavioural hunt — 737 Chrome VPN Extensions Caught Routing Traffic Through Proxies. Check If You H
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Browser egress to Myxa SOCKS5 proxy infrastructure (known IPs) · [LLM] DNS/connection to Myxa fake-VPN impersonation domains · [LLM] Browser-initiated SOCKS5 to TCP/1082 — new proxy infrastructure · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Browser egress to Myxa SOCKS5 proxy infrastructure (known IPs) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts endpoints whose browser (or any process) connects to the 20 confirmed SOCKS5 relay IPs operated by the Myxa fake-VPN extension cluster. Because 520 of 522 malicious extensions funnel the entire browser session to this shared infrastructure, an outbound flow to any of these IPs indicates a user is running one of the 737 impersonation VPN/proxy add-ons. Rationale: Uses the 20 confirmed SOCKS5 proxy IPs the article ties to '520 of 522' extensions routing browser traffic through the same infrastructure — direct-to-IP contact is a high-fidelity, low-FP signal independent of which impersonated brand the extension mimics.
ATT&CKT1090.002 T1176
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst detonating one of the extensions in a sandbox/VM on the corporate network
  • Threat-intel team actively validating these IOCs from a research egress
  • Decoy/honeypot host intentionally running the extension
  • A newly-provisioned corporate host in the same hosting provider range (e.g. 185.252.215.0/24, 178.130.47.0/24) reusing a recycled IP
  • Legitimate service unexpectedly sharing a multi-tenant IP with the proxy operator
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host/user and confirm the initiating process is a browser (chrome.exe/msedge.exe); enumerate installed Chrome extensions and check chrome.proxy.settings for a fixed SOCKS5 target on port 1082 with a loopback-only bypass list. 2) Contain: remove the offending extension, reset the browser proxy configuration to system default, and block the 20 proxy IPs at the egress firewall/proxy. 3) Hunt: pivot on all other hosts contacting any IP in the set or resolving the Myxa domain family; review the affected user's plaintext-HTTP browsing during the connected window (TLS SNI and any HTTP bodies were exposed AitM) and rotate credentials entered while the proxy was active.

DNS/connection to Myxa fake-VPN impersonation domains AICommand & Control High
Hunts resolution of or connection to the Myxa-cluster domains impersonating Proton VPN, NordVPN, Surfshark and others. These are the control/landing domains embedded in the malicious extensions and remote-config layer, distinct from the SOCKS5 relay IPs, providing a second independent pivot when the proxy IP set rotates. Rationale: The Myxa domain family (myxavpn.*, vpn-myxa.ru, plus brand-impersonation *.space domains) is the article's undisclosed-proxy control/landing infrastructure; DNS hits give a rotation-resistant pivot separate from the relay IPs in UC1.
ATT&CKT1090.002 T1176
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security-awareness or TI analyst browsing to a Myxa domain to inspect the fake VPN page
  • Sinkhole/DNS-RPZ infrastructure logging the query before blocking
  • Email/URL detonation sandbox visiting the domain
  • A user who genuinely believes they installed a real VPN and browses the vendor page
  • DNS resolver forwarder logging on behalf of many downstream clients (attribute to true client IP)
Response runbook
1) Triage: resolve the querying host/user and confirm whether a browser or the extension service worker triggered the lookup; check for a corresponding SOCKS5 flow to a port-1082 endpoint. 2) Contain: sinkhole/block the Myxa domain family at DNS and web proxy, and remove any impersonation VPN extension from the host. 3) Hunt: sweep DNS logs org-wide for the full domain list and for newly-registered *.space VPN-brand lookalikes; correlate hits with UC1 proxy-IP connections to build the full victim list and prioritise credential rotation for exposed users.

Browser-initiated SOCKS5 to TCP/1082 — new proxy infrastructure AICommand & Control Medium
Behavioural hunt for the defining Myxa technique: a browser routing its whole session to a fixed SOCKS5 server on port 1082. Excludes the already-known IOC IPs to surface NEW/rotated relay infrastructure beyond the 20 published addresses, since the operator runs a live subscription VPN business and cycles endpoints. Rationale: Port 1082 + browser-as-initiator is the article's defining behaviour ('chrome.proxy.settings to a fixed SOCKS5 server on port 1082'); excluding the 20 known IOC IPs turns this into a discovery hunt for rotated relay endpoints the published list misses.
ATT&CKT1090.002 T1176
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running a legitimate SSH dynamic SOCKS tunnel that happens to bind port 1082
  • A sanctioned corporate proxy/anti-censorship tool configured on TCP 1082
  • QA/pentest team testing a SOCKS5 client through the browser
  • Browser extension for a legitimate paid VPN that uses SOCKS5 on 1082
  • Security appliance doing TLS inspection re-originating browser flows on a non-standard port
Suppression filter
| where RemoteIP !in (dynamic([]))  // append sanctioned corporate SOCKS5 proxy IPs here to suppress known-good port-1082 endpoints
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each surfaced RemoteIP, WHOIS/geolocate and check for hosting-provider overlap with the known Myxa ranges; inspect the host's Chrome extensions and proxy settings for a loopback-only bypass list. 2) Contain: if the extension impersonates a known VPN brand and the bypass list is loopback-only, remove it, reset proxy config, and block the new IP at egress. 3) Hunt: add confirmed new IPs to the UC1 IOC set and to threat intel; sweep the org for other browsers hitting the same new endpoint and back-check exposed plaintext-HTTP traffic during connected windows.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Registry hive credential dump via reg.exe save/export (SAM/SECURITY/SYSTEM) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts reg.exe writing the HKLM\SAM, SECURITY, or SYSTEM hives to disk — the signature-light credential-access route the Picus Blue Report 2026 measured as blocked less than 1% of the time (vs ~94% for the classic LSASS route). This is the non-LSASS path defenders miss, not a generic LSASS-handle rule. Rationale: Uses the article's headline gap (registry hive read stopped <1%) with the exact reg.exe save/export + HKLM\SAM|SECURITY|SYSTEM cmdline pattern; ManageEngine and MITRE T1003.002 corroborate that this is the documented detection signature. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/002/ • https://www.picussecurity.com/blue-report • https://www.manageengine.com/log-management/correlation-rules/credential-theft-from-sam-via-registry-hive-dump.html • https://www.praetorian.com/blog/how-to-detect-and-dump-credentials-from-the-windows-registry/
ATT&CKT1003.002 T1003.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Backup/imaging software snapshotting SAM+SYSTEM (e.g. bare-metal recovery agents)
  • Administrator prepping an offline local-password reset (reg save HKLM\SAM)
  • DFIR/forensic acquisition tooling exporting hives during an authorized IR
  • OS migration/USMT tooling exporting the SYSTEM hive
  • Golden-image build scripts exporting registry hives
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("veeam.backup.shell.exe","wbengine.exe","vsnapvss.exe") and AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full ProcessCommandLine, parent process, user and integrity level; note the output file path (the .hiv/.reg target) and whether the user is a service/admin account expected to run backups. 2) Contain: if not an approved backup/IR action, isolate the host, force-rotate the local SAM account passwords/hashes and any domain accounts cached on that box, and preserve the dumped hive file. 3) Hunt: search the same host+adjacent hosts for follow-on secretsdump/impacket, the hive file being copied off-box or staged, and pass-the-hash/over-Kerberos logons using the recovered credentials.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "reg.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("save","export")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)hk(lm|ey_local_machine)\\(sam|security|system)"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\reg.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("save","export")
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)hk(lm|ey_local_machine)\\(sam|security|system)"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PowerShell command-history tampering (Clear-History / PSReadLine SaveNothing / ConsoleHost_history.txt deletion) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts clearing or disabling PowerShell console history — the single least-prevented technique in the Picus Blue Report 2026 (stopped 1% of the time). Fires on Clear-History, deletion of the PSReadLine ConsoleHost_history.txt file, or Set-PSReadLineOption -HistorySaveStyle SaveNothing. Rationale: Targets the article's standout stat (history-clearing stopped 1%) with the concrete PowerShell indicators (Clear-History, ConsoleHost_history.txt, HistorySaveStyle SaveNothing) rather than a generic defense-evasion template; T1070.003 confirms the mapping. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/003/ • https://www.picussecurity.com/blue-report
ATT&CKT1070.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer or power-user resetting their own PSReadLine history for privacy
  • Automation/CI runners disabling history persistence (HistorySaveStyle SaveNothing) by design
  • Admin scripts that Clear-History to avoid leaking secrets typed interactively
  • Endpoint hardening baselines that set SaveNothing via GPO/DSC
  • Roaming-profile cleanup deleting ConsoleHost_history.txt on logoff
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("gpscript.exe","CcmExec.exe") and AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm who/what launched it (interactive user vs script/automation), the parent process, and whether it coincides with other post-compromise activity on the host. 2) Contain: if unexplained, capture volatile data (running processes, network, scheduled tasks) before the actor cleans further, and snapshot the host; do not reboot (history/memory artifacts). 3) Hunt: pivot on the same host/user for the actions the history-wipe is hiding — recon bursts, reg.exe hive dumps (see registry-dump UC), new services, and outbound C2 in the surrounding window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "Clear-History"
    or (ProcessCommandLine has "ConsoleHost_history.txt" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Remove-Item","Clear-Content","del ","erase ","rm "))
    or (ProcessCommandLine has "HistorySaveStyle" and ProcessCommandLine has "SaveNothing")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
| where CommandLine has "Clear-History"
    or (CommandLine has "ConsoleHost_history.txt" and CommandLine has_any ("Remove-Item","Clear-Content","del ","erase "))
    or (CommandLine has "HistorySaveStyle" and CommandLine has "SaveNothing")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PowerShell Command History Tampering (Clear-History / PSReadLine)
id: c1a8e4d2-7b63-4f10-9a5e-2d8f16b4c0a7
status: experimental
description: Detects clearing or disabling PowerShell console history, the single least-prevented technique (1%) in the Picus Blue Report 2026, via Clear-History, deletion of ConsoleHost_history.txt, or Set-PSReadLineOption -HistorySaveStyle SaveNothing.
references:

  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/003/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/08/18
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1070.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_clear:

source:windows.security @EventID:4688 (@CommandLine:*Clear-History* OR @CommandLine:*clear-history* OR (@CommandLine:*ConsoleHost_history.txt* AND (@CommandLine:*Remove-Item* OR @CommandLine:*Clear-Content* OR @CommandLine:*del* OR @CommandLine:*erase*)) OR (@CommandLine:*HistorySaveStyle* AND @CommandLine:*SaveNothing*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i
| (CommandLine=/Clear-History/i OR (CommandLine=/ConsoleHost_history\.txt/i AND CommandLine=/(Remove-Item|Clear-Content|del |erase )/i) OR (CommandLine=/HistorySaveStyle/i AND CommandLine=/SaveNothing/i))
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count(as=execCount))
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process="*Clear-History*" OR (Processes.process="*ConsoleHost_history.txt*" AND (Processes.process="*Remove-Item*" OR Processes.process="*Clear-Content*" OR Processes.process="*del *" OR Processes.process="*erase *")) OR (Processes.process="*HistorySaveStyle*" AND Processes.process="*SaveNothing*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Internal domain reconnaissance burst (net view/share/session, nltest, session enum) AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts a single authenticated user/host firing 3+ distinct domain-mapping and share/session-enumeration commands within an hour — the least-prevented category in the Picus Blue Report 2026 (stopped ~10%). Correlates net.exe view/share/session/group, nltest domain queries, and quser/qwinsta session enumeration to surface the quiet pre-breach mapping stage. Rationale: Encodes the article's least-prevented category (recon/share+session enum stopped ~10%) as a distinct-command-type burst rather than alerting on any single benign net.exe; the 3-distinct-categories/hour threshold separates deliberate domain mapping from one-off admin lookups. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1135/ • https://www.picussecurity.com/blue-report
ATT&CKT1135 T1049 T1018 T1087.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Logon/GPO startup scripts running net use/net share/net view across a fleet
  • Asset-inventory or discovery tools (SCCM, Lansweeper) enumerating shares and sessions
  • Help-desk staff running quser/qwinsta to find and shadow user sessions
  • Domain-join or health-check scripts calling nltest /dclist or /dsgetdc
  • Backup software enumerating open sessions before a snapshot
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("gpscript.exe","CcmExec.exe","lansweeper.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the make_set of commands and the launching account — is it a known admin/service context or a standard user suddenly enumerating the domain? Check the parent process (interactive shell vs logon script). 2) Contain: if it's a non-admin user or an unusual host, scope the account's recent logons and step up monitoring; if paired with credential-dump or history-wipe signals, isolate the host and disable the account. 3) Hunt: from the same host/user, look forward for lateral movement (SMB/service exec), Kerberoasting, and the reg.exe hive dump / Clear-History behaviors from the sibling UCs within the surrounding window.
let Window = 1h;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName in~ ("net.exe","net1.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("view","share","session","group","localgroup"))
    or (FileName =~ "nltest.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dclist","/domain_trusts","/dsgetdc"))
    or (FileName in~ ("quser.exe","qwinsta.exe"))
| extend ReconType = case(
    FileName =~ "nltest.exe", "nltest",
    FileName in~ ("quser.exe","qwinsta.exe"), "session-enum",
    ProcessCommandLine has "view", "net-view",
    ProcessCommandLine has "share", "net-share",
    ProcessCommandLine has "session", "net-session",
    ProcessCommandLine has_any ("group","localgroup"), "net-group",
    "net-other")
| summarize DistinctReconTypes = dcount(ReconType), ReconTypes = make_set(ReconType), Commands = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 20), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, Window)
| where DistinctReconTypes >= 3   // 3+ distinct enumeration categories in 1h = deliberate domain mapping, not a one-off admin lookup
| order by LastSeen desc
let Window = 1h;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventID == 4688
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where (NewProcessName has_any ("\\net.exe","\\net1.exe") and CommandLine has_any ("view","share","session","group","localgroup"))
    or (NewProcessName has "\\nltest.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("/dclist","/domain_trusts","/dsgetdc"))
    or (NewProcessName has_any ("\\quser.exe","\\qwinsta.exe"))
| extend ReconType = case(
    NewProcessName has "nltest.exe", "nltest",
    NewProcessName has_any ("quser.exe","qwinsta.exe"), "session-enum",
    CommandLine has "view", "net-view",
    CommandLine has "share", "net-share",
    CommandLine has "session", "net-session",
    CommandLine has_any ("group","localgroup"), "net-group",
    "net-other")
| summarize DistinctReconTypes = dcount(ReconType), ReconTypes = make_set(ReconType), Commands = make_set(CommandLine, 20), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, SubjectUserName, bin(TimeGenerated, Window)
| where DistinctReconTypes >= 3   // 3+ distinct enumeration categories in 1h
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 ((@Image:(*\\net.exe OR *\\net1.exe OR *\\NET.EXE) AND (@CommandLine:*view* OR @CommandLine:*share* OR @CommandLine:*session* OR @CommandLine:*group* OR @CommandLine:*localgroup*)) OR (@Image:(*\\nltest.exe OR *\\NLTEST.EXE) AND (@CommandLine:*/dclist* OR @CommandLine:*/domain_trusts* OR @CommandLine:*/dsgetdc*)) OR @Image:(*\\quser.exe OR *\\qwinsta.exe OR *\\QUSER.EXE))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\\net1?\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(view|share|session|group|localgroup)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\nltest\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(\/dclist|\/domain_trusts|\/dsgetdc)/i) OR ImageFileName=/\\(quser|qwinsta)\.exe$/i
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| case { ImageFileName=/nltest/i => ReconType := "nltest"; ImageFileName=/(quser|qwinsta)/i => ReconType := "session-enum"; CommandLine=/view/i => ReconType := "net-view"; CommandLine=/share/i => ReconType := "net-share"; CommandLine=/session/i => ReconType := "net-session"; CommandLine=/(group|localgroup)/i => ReconType := "net-group"; * => ReconType := "net-other"; }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function=count(field=ReconType, distinct=true, as=DistinctRecon))
| DistinctRecon >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Processes.process) as commands min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name IN ("net.exe","net1.exe") AND (Processes.process="*view*" OR Processes.process="*share*" OR Processes.process="*session*" OR Processes.process="*group*" OR Processes.process="*localgroup*")) OR (Processes.process_name="nltest.exe" AND (Processes.process="*/dclist*" OR Processes.process="*/domain_trusts*" OR Processes.process="*/dsgetdc*")) OR (Processes.process_name IN ("quser.exe","qwinsta.exe"))) by Processes.dest Processes.user _time span=1h
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where NOT like(user,"%$")
| eval recon_count=mvcount(commands)
| where recon_count>=3
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as commands min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name IN ("net.exe","net1.exe") AND (Processes.process="*view*" OR Processes.process="*share*" OR Processes.process="*session*" OR Processes.process="*group*" OR Processes.process="*localgroup*")) OR (Processes.process_name="nltest.exe" AND (Processes.process="*/dclist*" OR Processes.process="*/domain_trusts*" OR Processes.process="*/dsgetdc*")) OR (Processes.process_name IN ("quser.exe","qwinsta.exe"))) by Processes.dest Processes.user _time span=1h
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where NOT like(user,"%$")
| eval recon_count=mvcount(commands)
| where recon_count>=3
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Adobe Patches Three CVSS 10.0 ColdFusion and Campaign Classic Flaws

The Hacker News
2026-08-12 6 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Adobe has shipped updates to address multiple critical security vulnerabilities impacting ColdFusion, Commerce, and Campaign Classic that, if successfully exploited, could result in arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation. The most severe of the flaws are listed below - CVE-2026-48362 (CVSS score: 10.0) - An operating system command injection vulnerability in ColdFusion that could

CVEsCVE-2026-48362 CVE-2026-48273 CVE-2026-71384 CVE-2026-71362 CVE-2026-71398 CVE-2026-27302 CVE-2026-48381 CVE-2026-48449

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] ColdFusion server process spawning OS shell / LOLBin (CVE-2026-48362 / CVE-2026-48273 RCE) · [LLM] Exposure: unpatched Adobe ColdFusion / Campaign Classic (APSB26-90 & APSB26-120 CVEs) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
ColdFusion server process spawning OS shell / LOLBin (CVE-2026-48362 / CVE-2026-48273 RCE) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the post-exploitation footprint of the two ColdFusion arbitrary-code-execution flaws Adobe patched in APSB26-90 (CVE-2026-48362 OS command injection, CVE-2026-48273 eval injection): the ColdFusion JVM/service process (coldfusion.exe, jrun.exe, cfexec.exe, or java.exe running the cfusion instance) spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell, or download/recon LOLBins. A web-app server launching an interactive shell is the highest-fidelity signal of RCE against ColdFusion since no exploit URI or payload string was published. Rationale: Grounded in APSB26-90's explicit vuln classes for CVE-2026-48362 (OS command injection) and CVE-2026-48273 (eval injection); with no published exploit URI/payload, the ColdFusion JVM parent -> shell/LOLBin child lineage is the deployable RCE tell. Cross-checked against SecurityWeek and Field Effect write-ups and the Adobe bulletin. Cross-checked against: • https://helpx.adobe.com/security/products/coldfusion/apsb26-90.html • https://www.securityweek.com/adobe-urges-immediate-patching-of-critical-coldfusion-campaign-classic-flaws/ • https://fieldeffect.com/blog/adobe-patches-coldfusion-campaign-classic
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.003 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate ColdFusion apps using the <cfexecute> tag to shell out to cmd.exe/net.exe for business logic
  • ColdFusion scheduled tasks or Event Gateways invoking PowerShell/cmd on a cadence
  • ColdFusion hotfix/updater or installer processes launching cmd.exe during patch application
  • Java-based build/monitoring agents co-located on the box where java.exe path incidentally contains a ColdFusion folder
  • Admin-run diagnostics (whoami/net) launched from a ColdFusion admin console feature
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("hf-2023", "hf-2025", "hotfix", "cfusion\\bin\\coldfusion.exe -stop") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "ColdFusion Add-on Services")
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the child ProcessCommandLine for download (certutil/curl/bitsadmin), recon (whoami/net/nltest), or encoded PowerShell; confirm the parent path resolves to a real ColdFusion install (\cfusion\ or \ColdFusionYYYY\) and note the service identity it ran as. 2) Contain: network-isolate the host, suspend the ColdFusion service, and preserve the JVM process; if commands are attacker-driven, rotate the ColdFusion service-account and datasource credentials. 3) Hunt: scan the ColdFusion wwwroot/CFIDE/admin webroots for newly written .cfm/.jsp web shells, review IIS/Apache/ColdFusion access logs for the request that preceded the spawn, and check DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound C2 from the ColdFusion process. Confirm the box is on 2025.0.12 / 2023.0.23.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("coldfusion.exe","jrun.exe","cfexec.exe","java.exe","javaw.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("ColdFusion","cfusion","JRun") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ColdFusion","cfusion","coldfusion") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("coldfusion.exe","jrun.exe","cfexec.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","nltest.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

Exposure: unpatched Adobe ColdFusion / Campaign Classic (APSB26-90 & APSB26-120 CVEs) AIExploitation High
Surfaces hosts still carrying the eight critical Adobe CVEs disclosed in the article so the SOC can prioritize the 72-hour Priority-1 patch window: the ColdFusion RCE/DoS set (CVE-2026-48362, CVE-2026-48273, CVE-2026-71384), Commerce privilege-escalation (CVE-2026-71362), and the Campaign Classic RCE/SQLi set (CVE-2026-71398, CVE-2026-27302, CVE-2026-48381) plus the prior CVE-2026-48449. Article-specific because it keys on the exact CVE IDs, not a generic 'outdated software' rule. Rationale: Uses the exact eight CVE IDs Adobe disclosed (validated against Adobe APSB26-90/APSB26-120 and NVD); a CVE-ID-scoped TVM query is deployable as-is and prioritizes the Priority-1 72h window the article calls out. No IOCs existed to ship since no exploitation is known. Cross-checked against: • https://helpx.adobe.com/security/products/coldfusion/apsb26-90.html • https://helpx.adobe.com/security/products/campaign/apsb26-120.html • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-71398
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Adobe-hosted / cloud Campaign Classic instances flagged by TVM even though Adobe already remediated them (only on-prem components need action)
  • Hosts already patched to ColdFusion 2025.0.12 / 2023.0.23 but with a stale TVM snapshot not yet refreshed
  • Dev/test ColdFusion boxes that are not internet-facing and lower priority than production
  • Software inventory version-parsing quirks reporting a hotfix-applied build as still vulnerable
Response runbook
1) Triage: rank returned hosts by internet exposure (IsInternetFacing in DeviceInfo) and severity, and confirm whether each is on-prem ColdFusion/Campaign Classic vs an Adobe-hosted instance that needs no action. 2) Contain: fast-track patching to ColdFusion 2025.0.12 / 2023.0.23 and Campaign Classic ACC v7 7.4.4 build 9400 within the 72h Priority-1 window; where patching lags, restrict admin endpoints at the WAF/network layer. 3) Hunt: on any internet-facing host still vulnerable, pivot to the companion ColdFusion-spawns-shell detection and review web-server access logs for anomalous POSTs to admin/API endpoints predating the patch.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has

// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-59310", "CVE-2026-59309")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33634")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33634")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
